newsitem.title: CHILE: Early Chile stock rise flags on electricity fears.
newsitem.headline: Early Chile stock rise flags on electricity fears.

text.p: An early rally in Chilean shares petered out mid-morning as electricity stocks sank on reports the government will impose power rationing as a result of this year's drought, said traders.
The 40-share .IPSA index was off 0.14 mid-morning at 118.32 points.
Investors were awaiting the outcome of a meeting Monday morning of the National Energy Commission, Chile's equivalent of an energy ministry, to decide on the rationing, they said.
Media reports at the weekend said the authorities will impose measures this month, including reducing power voltage and cutting lighting in public places.
Power output from Chile's dams, the country's main source of energy, has fallen steeply because of the drought.
"It will have to rain a lot for the situation to normalize. It is very, very difficult for electricity companies," said one trader.
Enersis was off 1.99 percent at 258 pesos, while Endesa lost 1.33 percent to 259 pesos.
The bolsa was also undermined by profit-taking on news of the Central Bank's widely exepected decision to cut interest rates Friday, said dealers.
The bourse has rallied strongly in the last two weeks on hopes of a rate cut.
